extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent search staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, evaluating, and searching prior art and for classification of patent applications, including what documents qualify as references, how to select search tools, and documentation/handling procedures. Primarily directed to patent examiners performing initial and continuing searches and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled matter in U.S. patent files
rubrics_metrics.description: Canceled matter in the application file of a U.S. patent or U.S. application publication is not a proper reference as of the filing date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canceled matter may be used as prior art as of the patent or publication date (it then constitutes prior public knowledge under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)). See cited cases (Ex parte Stalego; In re Lund) and MPEP §§ 2127, 2136.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned applications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned application published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and 102(b) as of its publication date; may be prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of the earliest effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpublished abandoned applications may be made available to the public under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv) and subject matter available to the public under 37 CFR 1.11(a) may be used as prior art as of the date it became publicly available. See MPEP § 2128 and § 2127.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending (unpublished) applications confidentiality and limited use
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending U.S. applications that have not been published are generally preserved in confidence (37 CFR 1.14(a)) and are not available as references, except as provided by specific regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in one nonprovisional application may be rejected on claimed subject matter of a copending nonprovisional application of the same inventive entity. AIPA (1999) rules require publication of most applications 18 months after earliest filing date, with enumerated exceptions (no longer pending, secrecy order, provisional application, design patent application, reissue). Applicants may request nonpublication (MPEP § 1122). See MPEP §§ 804, 2127.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. patents as prior art (effective date rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The face patent date (date of patenting) is usually cited, but the filing date is ordinarily the effective date as a reference (35 U.S.C. 102(e)); earlier effective U.S. filing dates (e.g., benefit of provisional or prior U.S. filings) may control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must determine the proper effective date of a U.S. patent (including claims to earlier priority) when using it as prior art. See MPEP §§ 706.02(f)(1), 2127. Examples: reissue patents use effective date of original application; patents issuing from applications claiming a provisional may have 102(e) date as provisional filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent document series and citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Different series of U.S. patents (X-series, 1836 series, Reissue, A.I., Plant, Design) have specific citation conventions and implications for reference dating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: X-series patents (1790–1836) should be cited by patentee name and date, not number; reissue patents must include 'Re.' prefix; plant patents use 'P.P.'; design patents use 'D.' See MPEP for details on identification and effective reference dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kind codes (WIPO ST.16) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO ST.16 kind codes (letter and sometimes number) distinguish kind of patent document and level of publication (e.g., A1, B1, C1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify USPTO documents by country code, patent/publication number, and kind code (e.g., 'US 7,654,321 B1' or 'US 2003/1234567 A1'). Tables list codes in use and legacy codes; see WIPO ST.16 and MPEP § 901.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: INID codes for bibliographic identification
rubrics_metrics.description: INID Codes provide internationally agreed numbers to identify bibliographic data on the first page of patent documents, enabling identification without knowledge of language or local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INID codes are applied to U.S. patents since Aug. 4, 1970. See list in MPEP § 901.05(b) for relevant INID codes and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent documents are usable only after date confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign patent, its application contents, or segments should not be cited as a reference until its date of patenting or publication can be confirmed by an examiner’s review of a copy of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be mindful of delays between grant and publication in some countries. Use STIC and available databases to confirm dates. See MPEP § 707.05(e) for data used in citing foreign references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of foreign patent equivalents in U.S. search files
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, one family member (priority earliest patent) was placed in examiners’ files; beginning October 1995, paper copies of foreign patents were no longer classified into the U.S. Classification System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior practice selected a prioritized country member for placement; foreign equivalents may still appear for older documents. See MPEP § 901.05 for search procedures for recently issued foreign patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent law variations affecting reference dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication/grant events (grant, publication, laying open, abstracts) occur differently among countries; these differences affect which date constitutes a 'printed publication' or other prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand country practice: some lay open for inspection, some publish specifications 18 months after filing, some publish notices in official journals, some issue patents of addition. Examiner should identify the applicable event/date that makes the material public and thus prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding specifications and patent family analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: A family of patents (same invention in multiple countries) may include documents with identical, translated, or varied disclosures; priority claims may affect earliest effective dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check corresponding family members for earlier publications/issues and verify whether earlier family members disclose the subject matter needed for a rejection. Use DWPI, INPADOC, Chemical Abstracts, WPI, and STIC for family tracing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and evidentiary weight of dates on foreign documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Office copies of foreign documents in the USPTO possession are prima facie evidence of the date or facts shown (28 U.S.C. 1745); examiners need only state the date of receipt when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In court, certified copies are prima facie evidence; applicants may rebut with competent evidence but this is rare. Consult STIC staff if earlier effective dates are crucial to a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and use of English versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicate or substantially duplicate foreign language specifications may exist in English or other languages; a translation may be cited for convenience but the reference content is determined by the document actually used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If citing an English translation, ensure it is a true translation and that questions of content are resolved based on the original specification used as the reference. Translational discrepancies should be resolved by reference to the original doc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpatent literature (NPL) as a reference source
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonpatent publications (scientific, technical literature, abstracts, defensive publications) are legitimate reference sources and must be considered in searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STIC, subject-specific databases, and trained search personnel for NPL. In arts where patents lag, NPL can be crucial. Document and include relevant NPL in search results and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC)
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC provides access to databases (Chemical Abstracts, DWPI/WPI, INPADOC), borrowed publications, and trained NPL search personnel to assist examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consult STIC for specialized searches, foreign patent info, and translation/abstracting resources. STIC may perform searches or provide access to databases not directly available to examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications are prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Published abstracts, abbreviatures, defensive publications, and statutory invention registrations are references and can be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)/(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct dating and confirm availability to the public. See MPEP § 901.06(d) and Chapter 1100 for statutory invention registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of art in Technology Centers and classification collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examination resources are arranged by Technology Centers and include class/subclass definitions, cross-reference art collections, digests, and other organized systems of literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining the field of search, consult Technology Center-specific supplemental guidance, cross-reference art collections, and class/subclass digests to ensure comprehensive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borrowing and obtaining references and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may obtain copies of documents (domestic and foreign) via Office resources, STIC, Files Repository, and through borrowing/publication services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures (e.g., 37 CFR 1.11(a) for copies of published applications and Office channels like PALM/IFW for file ordering). For foreign docs not in Office possession, use DWPI, INPADOC, or request STIC assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tools available and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A wide variety of manual and automated search tools (EAST, WEST, Cassis DVD-ROM, WPI, INPADOC, commercial databases) are available; choice depends on examiner knowledge, tool coverage, strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select tools based on art-specific needs (e.g., patent vs. NPL coverage), and combine tools (classification + text search) as appropriate. Use specialized tools for chemistry, DNA, etc., and consult ITRP/STIC when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual of Classification and use of class/subclass definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual of Classification, index to the U.S. Patent Classification System, class and subclass definitions, and definition notes guide proper classifying and searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources (and online Patent Classification home pages) to identify proper subclasses, cross-reference art collections, and to scope fields of search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of classification (statutory authority & scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification must follow statutory authority and principles: establish scope of class, establish subclasses and cross-reference art collections, and accommodate new/revised classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying, consider the scope of the class, cross-references, and whether new subclasses or reclassification are needed; monitor classification orders and reclassification alert reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifying and cross-referencing at allowance and during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifying and cross-referencing must be managed during prosecution including addition/deletion/transfer of patents and application publications, harmonized subclasses, and cross-referencing at allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep systematic notes during prosecution, coordinate transfers between Technology Centers when issuing in another center without transfer, and ensure cross-references are updated at allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and assignment procedures for new applications
rubrics_metrics.description: New applications must be classified and assigned to an examiner per USPTO procedures; procedures address immediate inspection of amendments, transfers, and general guidelines governing assignment of nonprovisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow local PALM/assignment systems and Technology Center-specific guidance for assignment and transfer. Ensure classification supports proper assignment and searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: International and Locarno classification usage
rubrics_metrics.description: International Patent Classification (IPC) and Locarno classifications provide international classification frameworks and designations for inventions and designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IPC and Locarno where applicable to supplement U.S. classification and for searching foreign patent literature and international publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of claims for search planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Search planning requires careful analysis of claims, consideration of variant embodiments within the scope of the claim, equivalents, and analogous arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search should cover claimed subject matter and disclosed features that might reasonably be expected to be claimed in amendments. Consider variant embodiments and equivalents when selecting search terms and classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of search determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining the field of search involves (A) identifying the field of search, (B) selecting proper tool(s), and (C) determining appropriate search strategies for each tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider domestic patents (including application publications), foreign patent documents, and NPL; do not eliminate any source without reasonable certainty no pertinent references exist there. Prioritize most-likely art areas first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified search expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper field of search normally includes the subclass where the claimed subject matter would be classified and all related subclasses, digests, and cross-reference art collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search from the largest combinations down to elementary parts; prioritize areas likely to contain the best references; consult other examiners or supervisory examiners for unfamiliar subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tool strategy (text vs classification and combinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated search tools usually provide both classification and text search capabilities; text search is powerful when terminology is established, but rarely sufficient alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine text searching with classification searching; use broader text terms and classification browsing in mechanical arts where shapes/spatial relations are important; use specialized tools for particular needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet searching policy for unpublished applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Organization users must restrict Internet search queries to the general state of the art when searching unpublished applications unless a secure link exists to protect confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-secure Internet activities that could disclose proprietary information for unpublished applications are not permitted. Document Internet search strategies per MPEP § 719.05 II.(F). See Internet Usage Policy (Article 9 & 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting search strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Search strategies (including Internet searches) must be documented in accordance with established Office practices and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document search queries, tools used, and rationale per MPEP § 719.05 II.(F) and Article 10 of the Internet Usage Policy. Proper documentation supports reproducibility and prosecution efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting a comprehensive search for first action
rubrics_metrics.description: A careful and comprehensive search, commensurate with the limitations appearing in the most detailed claims, should be made when preparing the first action on the merits so that subsequent actions may be final or allowance requires only updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search should cover claims and disclosed features that might be claimed later; applicants help by filing claims ranging from broad to more detailed. Use best references to forestall future broader claims; consult STIC/ITRP as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting and citing the 'best' prior art references
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is not required to cite all available references but should cite the 'best' reference(s); unnecessary multiplication of equivalent references should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare references carefully and cite those that most directly apply. If a best reference has a publication date < 1 year prior and may be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131, a secondary reference that cannot be overcome may be added. Fully consider applicant-submitted IDS references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specialized search assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: When search needs are complex (e.g., NPL, chemical structures, DNA sequencing), use trained professional online search personnel (ITRP/STIC) and specialized search tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are encouraged to use STIC/ITRP services for complex NPL searches or when specialized databases are required. Technology Centers may provide supplemental training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and retrieval of patented and abandoned files
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented and abandoned provisional and nonprovisional application files are ordered via PALM/IFW and Files Repository procedures; older files may be in remote warehouses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PALM transaction procedures, input required codes, and note response statuses (accepted, remote warehouse, not accepted, etc.). Use IFW to view many files electronically when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family information sources and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent family information is available via commercial databases (Derwent WPI, INPADOC) and automated search tools (EAST, WEST) and via STIC services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use family databases to find publication dates, family members, and earlier effective dates that might impact reference dating. WPI in-house is good for abstracts and IPC searches; INPADOC is useful for quick family/publication date checks.
